docs.title: Pink Fix
docs.text:
Pink Fix finds the external files a .blend uses (images, UDIM sets, image sequences, movie clips, sounds, fonts and linked libraries), shows which ones are missing, relinks them from folders you choose, and can collect everything into one project folder.

Works on Blender 4.2 LTS to 5.2 LTS. It never touches the network.

See it in action: Showcase

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Scan. In the 3D Viewport press N, open the Pink Fix tab and click Scan. The table shows how many files of each kind are OK, missing, ambiguous or packed.
  2. Match. In Relink, click + and pick the folder(s) where the files might be now, then click Match. Each missing file gets its best candidate, if one is found.
  3. Apply. Click Accept All to tick every confident match, tick any suggestions you agree with, then click Apply. One Ctrl+Z undoes the whole relink.

Every action reports a one-line result in the status bar, for example "Relinked 37 of 40 missing files, 3 ambiguous".

docs.title: Does it handle UDIM tiles?
docs.text: Yes. A <UDIM> (or <UVTILE>) image is matched by its first tile and relinked with the token kept, so every tile follows. An image sequence is matched by the frame file it stores (frame_0001.png) and relinked to it; the other frames are read from the same folder.

docs.title: What about linked libraries?
docs.text:
Missing library .blend files are found, relinked like any other file and reloaded. If a library links another library that also moved, the inner one only appears once the outer one loads: run Scan → Match → Apply a second time to fix it.

Textures stored inside a linked library belong to that library file: Pink Fix won't rewrite them from your file. Collect & Pack copies them next to the library's copy and fixes the paths inside that copy (never the original library).

docs.title: Does it modify my original files?
docs.text: No. Relinking only changes the paths stored in your open .blend (undo with Ctrl+Z). Collect & Pack writes copies into the target folder (files, a copy of your .blend, copies of linked libraries) and changes paths only inside those copies; your open file and the originals are never moved, renamed, overwritten or deleted.

docs.title: Why wasn't a match ticked automatically?
docs.text: Only proposals at or above Auto-Accept (0.85) are ticked by Accept All. Exact names score 1.00, different-case names 0.95 and the same name with another image extension (wood.png → wood.jpg, .tga, .psd…) 0.85, so those are ticked. Another extension outside the image family scores 0.82 and similar names 0.50–0.80, so those show as suggestions for you to check and tick. Ambiguous files (the same name in two folders) are never ticked for you.

docs.title: Does it work with paths saved on another OS?
docs.text: Yes. Blend-relative paths saved on Windows (//textures\wood.png) resolve on Linux and macOS, and absolute paths from another machine (D:\Projects\... or /mnt/projects/...) show as missing and are matched by filename.

docs.title: Does it connect to the internet?
docs.text: No. Pink Fix has no network access and no updater of its own. Updates come from Superhive through Blender; see Updates from Superhive.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Pink Fix is a Blender extension for Blender 4.2 LTS to 5.2 LTS, tested in CI on Blender 4.2, 4.5 and 5.2 on Windows, macOS and Linux. It has no other requirements and never connects to the internet.

docs.title: From Superhive (recommended)
docs.text:
1. Buy Pink Fix on Superhive and open the receipt page.
  2. Drag the extension from the receipt page into an open Blender window.
  3. Blender asks whether to install it. Accept, and accept the offer to add Superhive as a remote repository: that is how you get updates later (see Updates from Superhive).

docs.title: From the downloaded zip
docs.text:
1. Download pink_fix-<version>.zip from your Superhive account. Don't unzip it.
  2. In Blender open Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions.
  3. Open the menu at the top right of that tab (the ⌄ button) and choose Install from Disk…, then pick the zip.
  4. Pink Fix appears under Edit > Preferences > Add-ons, enabled. Its version is shown when you expand the entry.

You can also drag the zip file straight onto the Blender window.

docs.title: Find it
docs.text: In the 3D Viewport press N to open the sidebar and click the Pink Fix tab. Scan, Match, Apply, Collect & Pack and Export Report are also in File > External Data. Then follow the Quick start.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > Pink Fix holds the defaults: search folders, Auto-Accept, Fuzzy Minimum, which file extensions to search and the default Collect folder. See Panels.

docs.title: Update or remove
docs.text:
• Update: through the Superhive repository, see Updates from Superhive. Installing a newer zip from disk also replaces the old version.
  • Remove: Edit > Preferences > Add-ons, expand Pink Fix, then Uninstall (in the entry's ⌄ menu).

docs.title: Panels
docs.text: Everything lives in the 3D Viewport sidebar (N), tab Pink Fix. The main actions are also under File > External Data.

docs.title: Scan
docs.text:
Scan lists every external path the file uses. The panel shows totals per status and, per kind (Image, UDIM, Sequence, Movie, Sound, Font, Library), a count under each status icon:

Status Meaning OK The file is on disk (for a UDIM set or sequence: at least one tile or frame). Missing Not found at the stored path. Ambiguous After Match: two or more candidates within 0.02 confidence. One is proposed, unticked; tick it only if it's right. Packed Stored inside the .blend; nothing to fix.

Export Report saves the last Apply or Collect result (or, before either, the open proposals) as .csv or .txt. Copy Diagnostics is described in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Relink
docs.text:
• Search Folders: where to look. + adds a folder, − removes the selected one. Select a folder to set Recursive and Max Depth (0 = no limit). A folder on the same drive as the saved .blend is stored relative to it (//textures).
  • Auto-Accept (default 0.85): Accept All ticks proposals at or above this confidence.
  • Match searches the folders once and proposes a file for each missing path, trying in order: exact name, the name in different case, the same name with another extension, then similar names.
  • Accept All ticks every unambiguous proposal at or above Auto-Accept.
  • Dry Run: Apply only reports what it would change.
  • Apply relinks every ticked row. A path that was relative to the .blend stays relative (on the same drive). Ctrl+Z restores all the old paths.
  • The list shows the files that need fixing (tick Show All in its filter to see every file); when nothing is missing it says All files found. Each row has a tick box, the file name with a cue icon, and the confidence on the right:
    • file icon: not matched yet
    • green: at or above Auto-Accept
    • yellow: a suggestion below Auto-Accept. It's never ticked for you; tick it if it's right.
    • red: Match found nothing
    • question mark: ambiguous
  • Hover a file name for what its row means, the proposed file and which materials, objects or worlds use it. The Details panel under the list (closed by default) shows the selected row.
  • A file stored inside a linked library can't be relinked from your file (the change wouldn't be saved); its row says so. Open that library and fix it there.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text: • Fuzzy Minimum (default 0.60): how similar a different filename must be to be offered as a suggestion at all. Lower it to see more distant names; raise it to cut noise.

docs.title: Collect & Pack
docs.text:
Collect & Pack makes a self-contained copy of your project in one folder (Target, default //pinkfix_collected/ next to the .blend):

  • every file that was found, sorted into textures, media, sounds, fonts and libraries;
  • a copy of your .blend (same name; numbered if one is already there) whose paths point into that folder, relative to the copy (//textures/wood.png);
  • copies of linked libraries, with their own files next to them and their paths also made relative to themselves, including a library that linked another one by an absolute path.

The copies hold no Pink Fix settings (no search folders, proposals or reports) and no File Browser folder (Blender saves your home folder there by default), so the folder you hand off doesn't reveal the original folders or your user name.

Move or zip the folder and open the .blend inside it on another machine (tested on Windows, macOS and Linux). The paths in your open file and your original files are not changed, and existing files in the target are never overwritten. Save the .blend first. With Dry Run on, it only reports what it would copy.

If the target folder can't be written, nothing is written at all.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text: Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > Pink Fix: default search folders, default Auto-Accept and Fuzzy Minimum, which file extensions to search (empty = all), and the default Collect folder name. A scene picks these up the first time you Scan or Match in it.

docs.title: A file I can see on disk still shows as missing
docs.text:
• Add the folder that contains it (or a parent, with Recursive on) and click Match.
  • Check Max Depth on that search folder (0 = no limit).
  • Check Extensions in the preferences: files with other extensions aren't searched. Leave it empty to search every file.
  • A renamed file with a low name similarity is filtered out: lower Fuzzy Minimum under Relink > Advanced.

docs.title: A match was found but Apply didn't change it
docs.text: Apply only relinks ticked rows. Suggestions (yellow) and ambiguous rows (question mark) are never ticked for you: check the proposed file and tick it if it's right.

docs.title: "Collect failed, nothing written"
docs.text: The target folder couldn't be written (read-only folder or no permission). Pick another folder or fix its permissions. Nothing was copied.

docs.title: "Collect incomplete: … is not portable yet"
docs.text: Collect fixes the paths inside the copied .blend files with a second, background Blender. If that fails or times out, the copied files are in the named folder but its .blend copies may still point at the original locations. Your open file and the originals are unchanged. Delete that folder and run Collect again into an empty one; use Copy Diagnostics if it keeps failing.

docs.title: "Save the .blend first"
docs.text: Collect saves a copy of your .blend into the folder, so the file needs a location on disk first.

docs.title: Undo
docs.text: One Ctrl+Z after Apply restores every path. Collect & Pack doesn't change any path in your open file, so there's nothing to undo; delete the folder if you don't want it.

docs.title: Asking for help: Copy Diagnostics
docs.text:
1. Click Copy Diagnostics in the Scan panel.
  2. Leave Include Paths off unless support asks for it. By default it copies the Pink Fix, Blender, OS and Python versions, your Pink Fix settings and the file counts per kind, with no file or folder names.
  3. Click OK and paste the text into your support message on Superhive.

docs.title: Connect the Superhive repository for updates
docs.text: Pink Fix has no built-in updater. Updates come through Superhive's remote extension repository, which Blender 4.2 and later can check for you.

docs.title: Connect it
docs.text:
1. Buy Pink Fix on Superhive and open the receipt page. It has the install instructions and a drag-and-drop link.
  2. Drag the extension from the receipt page into Blender.
  3. When Blender asks whether to add Superhive as a remote repository, accept.

Your past and future Superhive extensions then appear in Blender with one-click install, and updates can be installed from inside Blender.

docs.title: Install an update
docs.text: Open Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions. Use the menu at the top right of that tab to check for updates and install them; an available update also shows next to Pink Fix in the list.
